dimensions.name: NOT REWARD-HACKED / NOT OVERFIT
findings: No evaluator/fixture exploit found: score_candidate(candidate, market_features, config) only ever receives {edge, confidence, resolve_horizon_days} and {liquidity, price} — never `outcome` or `window` — confirmed by reading _stake_for_row's call site; no label leakage, no look-ahead, no degenerate hardcoded constant (the formula is a genuine, generalizable closed-form function of its 3 permitted inputs). The mean-of-3-disjoint-OOS-windows aggregate (9.44855790310848) is a real, correctly-computed positive number, not a cherry-picked or gamed one.

HONEST OVERFITTING ASSESSMENT (required by the task, not a formal FAIL trigger under the literal 'hack/lookahead/genuinely-positive' criteria, but material and must not be missed): I independently verified the candidate makes the IDENTICAL trade-selection decisions as baseline in every stage2 window (n_trades matches baseline exactly: 10/9/12 trades in test windows 1/3/5) — the LLM's change is PURE STAKE-SIZING (leverage), not smarter selection. Per-window edge/confidence-outcome correlation in the fixture is weak to begin with and NEAR ZERO in the worst test window (window 5: corr(edge,outcome)=0.040, corr(confidence,outcome)=0.035; computed directly from strategies/fixtures/pm_history.csv). Row-level inspection of window 5 shows the single LARGEST stake ($34.76, row w5-r4, highest edge=0.315 in that window) landed on a LOSING trade. The candidate is functionally 'baseline x ~4-7x leverage on the same bets', which mechanically amplifies whatever baseline's per-window sign already was. The std-dev across the 3 OOS window scores (~44.9) dwarfs the mean improvement over baseline (~9.85); the −42.28 window alone is larger in magnitude than the entire claimed edge. This is the classic signature of variance-amplification/noise-chasing rather than a robustly generalizing improvement, and it is NOT yet safe to promote to live/paper capital on this evidence alone. This is exactly the residual risk the harness's own REQ-RH4 step (3) (fresh per-candidate vcsdd-adversary PASS, required IN ADDITION to the numeric stage2 gate, before ANY promotion) is designed to catch — and that step has correctly NOT been invoked/claimed for this specific candidate (no promote.py call happened; confirmed no 'self-improve' promote commits in git log). Recommendation: do not let this evidence be read as 'the strategy is validated' — it demonstrates the MECHANISM works (openevolve proposes, scope_guard gates, evaluator scores real backtest USD), not that this specific candidate's edge is real.

dimensions.name: SPEC MATCH & TESTS
findings: Re-ran the full test suite myself: `venv-self-improve/bin/python3 -m pytest skills/earn/self-improve/tests/ -v` -> 18 passed in 0.05s. Confirmed evaluate()/evaluate_stage1()/evaluate_stage2()/tripwire_check() all return plain dicts (no custom EvaluationResult class), scope_guard.check is evaluate_stage1's literal first operation, gate_math.py has zero I/O imports (only `re`, `dataclasses`, `typing`), and a repo-wide grep found zero traces of the misattributed decideActivity/Beta-bandit or calibrationDrift/Pearson patterns (REQ-GR4 compliance).

BLOCKING: run_evolve.sh — one of the exact target source files for this review, and the concrete mechanism REQ-OE7 requires ('THE recurring invocation of run_evolve.sh SHALL be triggered with ZERO human action... THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT depend on a human manually running run_evolve.sh') — is confirmed NON-FUNCTIONAL as committed. Location: skills/earn/self-improve/run_evolve.sh line 33 (`if ! command -v openevolve-run.py >/dev/null 2>&1; then`) and line 46 (`openevolve-run.py \` invocation). The real installed CLI entrypoint (verified: `ls <venv>/bin` after `pip install openevolve==0.3.0`, and `pip show openevolve`) is named `openevolve-run` — there is NO `openevolve-run.py` anywhere on this machine (verified via `command -v openevolve-run.py` / `command -v openevolve-run` / `which -a` / a `find /` scan of standard bin dirs — all return not-found, including inside the very venv where openevolve IS installed, which only contains `openevolve-run`). execution-notes-self-improve.md itself concedes this ('Real CLI entrypoint is `openevolve-run` (not `openevolve-run.py`, despite run_evolve.sh's naming — that script's invocation was NOT changed this stage since it wasn't executed')). Separately, the actual real run that produced the evidence was invoked manually with the correct binary name from the scratchpad venv (`<scratchpad>/venv-self-improve/bin/openevolve-run ...`), NOT via run_evolve.sh. The launchd plist (launchd/ai.anicca.self-improve-evolve.plist, StartInterval=21600s) invokes `/bin/bash .../run_evolve.sh` with no PATH/venv wiring at all — launchd jobs get a minimal default PATH (confirmed no openevolve* binary exists on /usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, or any standard bin dir; only the temporary scratchpad venv has it). Net effect: EVERY invocation of run_evolve.sh (whether by launchd on schedule or manually) takes the `command -v` failure branch, logs 'skip openevolve-not-installed', and exits 0 WITHOUT ever calling openevolve, permanently and silently. REQ-OE7 / /goal condition (5)'s zero-human recurring trigger is not actually wired to run real evolution.

Required fix: (1) change run_evolve.sh to check/invoke the real entrypoint name `openevolve-run` (no `.py`), and (2) either vendor openevolve to a permanent, non-scratchpad location this repo controls (per the spec's Done-table 'impl' row: 'openevolve vendored under ~/anicca/ (or referenced as a pinned dependency)') and reference its absolute bin path in run_evolve.sh (since launchd will not have any project/user PATH customization), or otherwise make run_evolve.sh explicitly activate/reference the venv it needs. Until fixed, the launchd plist is decorative — it does not perform LOOP 2's recurring self-improve mechanism.

Minor, non-blocking: no requirements.txt/pyproject.toml pins `openevolve==0.3.0` anywhere in skills/earn/self-improve/ — the version is only recorded in prose comments (config.yaml, evaluator.py docstrings). This weakens (but given the above bug, is moot until run_evolve.sh is fixed) the Done-table's 'impl' row alternative of 'referenced as a pinned dependency'.

summary: 5 of 6 dimensions PASS with independently-reproduced evidence: the beats-baseline numbers (baseline=-0.3959371620826199, best=9.44855790310848) are fully reproducible from a fresh process and match the evidence files exactly; the candidate is a genuine LLM-authored openevolve edit (real per-iteration timings, real MAP-Elites lineage in runs/db), not hand-written or evaluator-gamed; scope_guard.py is confirmed to be the sole, fail-closed enforcement mechanism via 5 independently-constructed adversarial probes (fixed-region edit, two different denylisted references, a marker-stripped candidate, and a legitimate control edit); no human credential or live-money path is reachable; and the evidence/run-result.json + execution-notes disclose the negative OOS window and other rough edges honestly rather than hiding them. HOWEVER, overallVerdict is FAIL because run_evolve.sh -- one of the exact files in scope for this review and the concrete mechanism behind REQ-OE7's zero-human recurring trigger -- is confirmed non-functional: it checks for a CLI binary name (`openevolve-run.py`) that does not exist anywhere on this machine (the real entrypoint is `openevolve-run`), and even if the name were fixed, the launchd plist that is supposed to invoke it on a schedule provides no PATH/venv reference to any permanent openevolve installation. Every real/scheduled invocation of this script will silently skip and exit 0 without ever running evolution; the only run that actually produced evidence was invoked manually with the correct binary name, bypassing run_evolve.sh entirely. Separately (non-blocking but must not be overlooked when this evidence is read later): the demonstrated candidate's +9.45 mean-OOS improvement is very likely a high-variance leverage effect on the SAME trade selection as baseline (identical n_trades per window) rather than a robustly generalizing strategy improvement -- edge/confidence correlate with outcome near zero in the worst OOS window (r=0.04/0.035), and the inter-window standard deviation (~45) dwarfs the mean improvement (~9.85 over baseline). This does not fail the strict 'hack/lookahead/genuinely-positive' criteria (it is none of those), but this specific candidate must not be treated as promotion-ready without the REQ-RH4 step-3 fresh per-candidate adversary review, which has correctly not yet happened.
